data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'lystera', which means 'reclining, resting, or lying'. In Greek mythology, Lystra was the name of a city and a goddess who was associated with fertility and childbirth.

in_hebrew.name: ליסטרא
in_hebrew.meaning: מקום ישיבה, שמות מקום, עיר, יישוב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ליסטרא היא שם עיר באסיה הקטנה, באזור הדרומי של אנטוליה. השם נזכר ביוחנן 14:6–8 כמקום בו לקחו את שאול לצורך טקס. שם עיר מקורי באסיה הקטנה, ששימש גם כשם איש. במקרא, השם ייחודי לשם העיר. כיום, נעשה שימוש בשם כשם איש. משמעות רוחנית: תושב, קבוצה של ישראלים, וכן, כל דבר שנוצר בעקבות ישראל.

in_greek.name: Λύστρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Λύστρα (Λύστρα) είναι πόλις στην Μικρά Ασία, αναφέρεται στο κατά Ιωάννην Ευαγγέλιο (14:6–8). Ονομασία της πόλεως από την αρχαία ελλάδα, που σημαίνει «οικισμός» ή «πόλις». Σημασία της πόλεως: οικισμός, πόλις, τόπος. Σημασία θρησκευτική: η πόλη Λύστρα είναι σημαντική για τους χριστιανούς, καθώς αναφέρεται στην ιστορία του Ευαγγελίου του Ιωάννη.

in_latin.name: Lystra
in_latin.long_meaning: Lystra, in antiquo Asia Minor, urbs est, in quo Paulo apostolo et Barnabae cum Philippo evangelizante, secundum Ioannis Evangelium (14:6–8), apparuit. Ubi in urbe, in templo Dionysii, ut in actis apostolorum (14:8–18), congregatio multiudine gentium congregata, ut in libro Actuum apostolorum (14:8-18), facta est. Ubi in urbe, sanctus Paulus, cum Barnaba, secundum Ioannis Evangelium (14:6–8), apparuit et percepit. Significatio urbis: vicus, civitas, locus, qui signat, locus, civitas, in qua apparuit sanctus Paulus.

in_english.name: Lystra
in_english.meaning: place of residence, city, settlement, location
in_english.long_meaning: Lystra is a city in ancient Asia Minor, referred to in the Gospel of John (14:6–8) as the location where Paul the Apostle and Barnabas met with Philip the Evangelist. The name Lystra is derived from the Greek word for 'settlement' or 'city'. In Christian tradition, Lystra is significant as the place where Jesus appeared to Paul and Barnabas. In terms of spiritual significance, Lystra represents a place of residence, city, or settlement, symbolizing a location where Jesus appears to His followers.

biblical_reference.note: In the Gospel of John, Lystra is mentioned as the location where Paul the Apostle and Barnabas met with Philip the Evangelist.

saint_reference.note: Lystra is not a saint's name, but rather a place mentioned in the Bible.

data.cultural_impact: In the New Testament, Lystra is mentioned as a city in ancient Lycaonia (modern-day Turkey), where the Apostles Paul and Barnabas preached and healed a crippled man. This event led to the conversion of many people in the region and brought Christianity to the area for the first time.
data.spiritual_significance: In a broader sense, the name Lystra can be seen as a reminder of the importance of rest and relaxation in our spiritual journey. Just as the crippled man was healed and able to walk again, we too must allow ourselves to rest and be healed spiritually. Additionally, the name can be seen as a symbol of the fertile ground of the human soul, ready to receive the seeds of faith and grow into a vibrant spiritual life.

historical_references.reference: Lystra was a city in Lycaonia, Anatolia, mentioned in the New Testament as the site of Paul's second missionary journey and the location of his healing of a cripple.

Lystra is also mentioned in the Classical Greek literature as the site of a famous oracle of Zeus. In ancient Greek mythology, it was believed that Zeus appeared to the Lycaonians in human form and was called 'Lycaeus' in their honor.
historical_references.context: Classical Greek Literature, Pausanias Description of Greece 8.52

modern_usage.modern_context: Lystra is a historical city located in the Anatolian region of Turkey. It's a popular tourist destination due to its rich history and biblical significance. You can find Lystra on Google Maps, where it's marked as a point of interest. In the tourism industry, Lystra is often included in historical tours of Turkey. Additionally, Lystra is commonly mentioned in geography textbooks as an important ancient city.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Lystra is derived from the Greek word 'lystra,' meaning 'wolfish' or 'wild.' In the New Testament, Lystra is the name of a city where Paul and Barnabas preached and healed a man who was lame. This event led to the people of Lystra mistakenly believing that Paul and Barnabas were gods, emphasizing the contrast between the wild, pagan culture and the transformative power of Christian faith.
